steps: A downstream consumer falls behind and its bounded queue approaches capacity.
It reduces credits, pauses reads, or returns overload.
Upstream producers slow, buffer within limits, or reject new work.
Queue depth stabilizes instead of growing until collapse.

lesson.scenario: A streaming pipeline slows producers when the indexing consumer cannot drain its bounded queue.
entities: Emits records at an adjustable rate

steps.title: Balanced flow
steps.narration: Producer and consumer both run at 250 records per second.
steps.invariant: The buffer is bounded; it cannot be the long-term capacity plan.

steps.title: Consumer slows
steps.narration: Indexing capacity falls to 100 per second while production remains 250.
steps.invariant: Backpressure should react before the queue is exhausted.

steps.title: High watermark
steps.narration: Depth reaches 820 and the meter withdraws most credits.
steps.outcome: Upstream receives an explicit saturation signal.
steps.invariant: Pressure must propagate to the producer rather than create unbounded memory growth.

steps.title: Producer slows
steps.narration: The producer reduces its rate below consumer recovery capacity.
steps.outcome: The consumer begins draining the backlog.
steps.invariant: When slowing is impossible, the system needs explicit rejection, shedding, or durable spillover.

steps.title: Low watermark recovery
steps.narration: Depth falls below 300 and credits gradually increase.
steps.outcome: Throughput returns without immediately recreating overload.
steps.invariant: Credit recovery should be gradual enough to avoid oscillation.
